summary.oneLiner: Earkart Limited is a technology-enabled healthcare and pharmaceutical product distributor that listed on the BSE SME platform on 03 October 2025.
summary.business: Earkart Limited is engaged in the distribution of healthcare and pharmaceutical products, facilitating their availability from manufacturers to healthcare providers and consumers through an efficient supply chain network. The Company positions itself on quality products, strong customer relationships and technology-driven processes that improve operational efficiency. It operates one wholly owned subsidiary, Earkart Inc. (USA), incorporated on 20 January 2026 and non-operational as of 31 March 2026.

endMarkets: India — pharmaceutical and healthcare product distribution / healthcare supply chain|United States of America — via wholly owned subsidiary Earkart Inc. (non-operational as of 31 March 2026)

currentContext.expansion: Earkart is an asset-light healthcare and pharmaceutical distributor and the annual report discloses no plants, capacity additions or project pipeline. Expansion in FY 2025-26 took the form of corporate rather than physical build-out: the Company completed its IPO and listed on the SME Platform of BSE Limited on 03 October 2025, and incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Earkart Inc., in the United States of America on 20 January 2026 as a platform to evaluate future international opportunities — the subsidiary remained non-operational as of 31 March 2026. Management states it continued to invest in strengthening operational infrastructure, technology capabilities and the compliance framework, and lists strengthening technology-led distribution capabilities and exploring international growth avenues through Earkart Inc. among its FY 2026-27 focus areas. No commissioning dates, site locations, capacity numbers or rupee capex quantum are disclosed; the named Capital Commitments disclosure states 'Nil'.

risks.risk: Regulatory risk in pharmaceutical and healthcare distribution
risks.note: Management states the sector is subject to extensive regulation and that changes in government policies, pricing controls, licensing requirements and compliance obligations may impact business operations.

risks.risk: Intense competition in a fragmented distribution market
risks.note: The Company operates in a highly competitive market with numerous regional and national participants; management says maintaining customer relationships and service quality remains critical.
Management flags disruptions in supply chains, transportation challenges, vendor dependency and fluctuations in logistics costs as risks to operational performance.

risks.risk: Logistics and operating cost inflation compressing margins
risks.note: Realised, not hypothetical: despite ~25% revenue growth, FY26 PBT and PAT both fell, which management attributed to increased logistics and transportation costs, higher operational and employee-related expenses, listing and compliance costs, and competitive market conditions.
Changes in macroeconomic conditions, inflationary pressures, interest rates and consumer spending patterns may influence business growth.
Increasing reliance on digital systems for a technology-driven distribution model requires continuous focus on information security, data protection and system reliability.

risks.risk: Compliance and control gaps at a newly listed SME
risks.note: The Secretarial Auditor raised observations on Structured Digital Database maintenance, cost records and overseas investment filing; the Company did not adequately maintain the cost records prescribed under the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014, and had not filed Form FC with the AD Banker for the US subsidiary under the FEMA Overseas Investment Rules, 2022, with Late Submission Fees now payable.

risks.risk: Unproven international expansion via a non-operational US subsidiary
risks.note: Earkart Inc. was incorporated on 20 January 2026 but remained non-operational at 31 March 2026 with nil share capital, assets and turnover per Form AOC-1, so the stated international growth avenue is at present a platform only and has already produced a FEMA filing lapse.

moat.title: Strengths (RHP)
moat.body:
- Efficient supply chain / distribution network for healthcare and pharmaceutical products connecting manufacturers to healthcare providers and consumers
- Technology-driven processes used to improve operational efficiency, inventory management, customer engagement and supply chain visibility
- Listed status on the BSE SME platform, which management states has enhanced visibility and strengthened its governance framework
- Positioned as an organised, professionally managed player as the healthcare distribution industry shifts towards organised and compliant distribution networks

risks.title: Risks (RHP)
risks.body:
- Management states the sector is subject to extensive regulation and that changes in government policies, pricing controls, licensing requirements and compliance obligations may impact business operations.
- The Company operates in a highly competitive market with numerous regional and national participants; management says maintaining customer relationships and service quality remains critical.
- Management flags disruptions in supply chains, transportation challenges, vendor dependency and fluctuations in logistics costs as risks to operational performance.
- Realised, not hypothetical: despite ~25% revenue growth, FY26 PBT and PAT both fell, which management attributed to increased logistics and transportation costs, higher operational and employee-related expenses, listing and compliance costs, and competitive market conditions.
- Changes in macroeconomic conditions, inflationary pressures, interest rates and consumer spending patterns may influence business growth.
- Increasing reliance on digital systems for a technology-driven distribution model requires continuous focus on information security, data protection and system reliability.
- The Secretarial Auditor raised observations on Structured Digital Database maintenance, cost records and overseas investment filing; the Company did not adequately maintain the cost records prescribed under the Companies (Cost Records and Audit) Rules, 2014, and had not filed Form FC with the AD Banker for the US subsidiary under the FEMA Overseas Investment Rules, 2022, with Late Submission Fees now payable.
- Earkart Inc. was incorporated on 20 January 2026 but remained non-operational at 31 March 2026 with nil share capital, assets and turnover per Form AOC-1, so the stated international growth avenue is at present a platform only and has already produced a FEMA filing lapse.
